harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Set up a LUKS2-encrypted file-backed volume on node1, mounted at /srv/secure, configured to auto-unlock via a root-only keyfile and auto-mount at boot through /etc/crypttab and /etc/fstab (systemd generators). Verified via a full node reboot that the volume unlocks and mounts with no manual intervention and data persists.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (Ubuntu 24.04) block devices; found no spare partition, so created a 2G file-backed LUKS2 volume at /var/lib/secure-volume/secure.img
Generated a root-only-readable keyfile at /root/keys/secure.key (chmod 600) for automatic unlock
Ran cryptsetup luksFormat (LUKS2) on the image file using the keyfile
Opened the LUKS volume as /dev/mapper/secure_srv, formatted ext4, mounted at /srv/secure, wrote a test file
Added /etc/crypttab entry (secure_srv, image path, keyfile path, luks,nofail) and /etc/fstab entry (/dev/mapper/secure_srv /srv/secure ext4 defaults,nofail)
Reloaded systemd, verified generated units (systemd-cryptsetup@secure_srv.service, srv-secure.mount) and that srv-secure.mount is pulled into local-fs.target automatically
Manually started the mount unit to confirm auto-unlock/mount works before rebooting
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, machine-id, uptime, mount status, file contents
Triggered systemctl reboot on node1 (single node, acknowledgement returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec was available again
Verified boot_id changed and uptime reset, confirming an actual restart occurred

Verified post-restart: systemd-cryptsetup@secure_srv.service succeeded automatically, srv-secure.mount is active, /srv/secure is mounted from /dev/mapper/secure_srv, and the pre-existing test file is present and readable

evidence.requirement: Encrypted volume created and mounted at /srv/secure
evidence.summary: cryptsetup luksFormat succeeded on the file-backed image, luksOpen succeeded creating /dev/mapper/secure_srv, ext4 was created and mounted at /srv/secure with a test file written and read back.

evidence.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts on its own at boot (pre-reboot proof of mechanism)
evidence.summary: Added crypttab entry referencing the keyfile and fstab entry for the mapper device; systemd generated systemd-cryptsetup@secure_srv.service and srv-secure.mount and pulled srv-secure.mount into local-fs.target automatically (no noauto/manual enable needed); manually starting the unit unlocked and mounted the volume successfully, proving the boot path works.
Captured pre-restart boot_id (f9bf293d-1eb8-423e-b185-84e94db646f3), machine-id, uptime, and confirmed srv-secure.mount active with data present, as the baseline for node1 (the only managed node).

Issued a backgrounded systemctl reboot that returned an acknowledgement before the node disconnected; the immediate follow-up exec confirmed the node was down (connection reset), proving the reboot actually occurred.

evidence.requirement: Node1 changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id read as e7733aa3-693a-4ae6-82d3-1fce6038a1db (different from the pre-restart f9bf293d-...) with a fresh uptime timestamp, proving a genuine restart rather than a service bounce.

evidence.requirement: Node1 post-restart recovery of encrypted volume and data
evidence.summary: After the restart, systemd-cryptsetup@secure_srv.service completed successfully with no manual action, srv-secure.mount is active, /srv/secure is mounted from /dev/mapper/secure_srv, and the pre-existing test file content ('hello') was read back intact, confirming automatic unlock, mount, and data integrity survive a reboot.
